title: Startup and host integration
invariant: Follow the host boundary: workspace identity scopes the mounted runtime; native panel navigation and DOM stay inside its host. Native panel sizing must fill the viewport remainder in HA’s auto-height wrapper while preserving sidebar flow and safe-area padding.

title: Project schema and persistence
invariant: Trace draft, published state and revision checks before changing persistence; preserve portable IDs and migrations. Opt-in outdoor platform rooms derive stable identities through platform-rooms; physical slabs, ceilings and roofs keep structural rooms separate. Personal GLBs are immutable SHA assets outside snapshots; references and record publication share a transaction. Unsupported fields and newer schema versions stay blocked and explain the HACS update, restart and reload recovery path. Weather source preferences are private and origin-scoped; their revision-checked save updates only that field in draft and published profiles. Rejected records surface blocking errors before warnings. Missing catalog models and variants stay warning-only through project and dashboard validation and retain their IDs, placements and slots; rendering uses placeholders or default variants. Editor Issues provides update/reimport guidance. Blocking dashboard screens keep Workspaces and complete workspace backup access, with technical details collapsed. Native HA library suggestions append only healthy remote homes missing locally and reuse identity-preserving, conflict-checked restore; discovery stays read-only. WorkspaceDeletion owns local/permanent deletion actions, backup and version-checked HA deletion without restore, including remote-only cards; local removal clears sync cursors. Library, settings and draft-recovery downloads share the complete archive owner, including verified staged GLBs; recovery exports the live draft and private mappings without overwriting a newer record.

title: Editor coordination
invariant: Keep mode coordination separate from domain edits, history, persistence and presentation; Apply is the publication boundary. Save proceeds directly for warnings or no issues; errors and failed saves open the review dialog. Shared draft diagnostics remain available in every editor mode; Locate selects and focuses the affected object on its floor, including wall attachments. Construct and Arrange share ordered 3D/2D/Explore controls and Shift+1/2/3 shortcuts; Construct disables 3D. View shortcuts respect typing, dialogs and unfinished edits, and reuse Explore pointer lock. Keep tools and catalog on the left, automatically selected Properties on the right and collapsible Issues below the canvas. Property collapse preserves selection; panel changes wait for active gestures. Full-height Properties overlays preserve canvas bounds and camera projection. Undo/Redo share project actions with Reset/Save. Shared flat form styling retains semantic groups and focus. Mobile Construct and Arrange start with a compact dock and closed panels. EditorPanels owns a full-screen native dialog with focus containment, Escape/Done dismissal and one underlined active tab. Canvas selection leaves mobile panels closed; successful catalog insertion, tool choice and canvas tasks dismiss them. Phone landscape uses the same pattern. Panel state stays outside project persistence. Scene-item Issues rows identify the model and expose Select in Arrange, Reset placement and Remove. Item removal uses itemBindingSlotIds to clean draft controls, readings and lighting even during unfinished geometry, preserving published mappings and Undo. Failed exits retain the in-memory draft, show storage/conflict recovery and reset pending navigation for explicit retries. Settings replaces the Shortcuts tab and keeps section navigation in the editor sidebar. Settings routes and legacy Home Assistant/Shortcuts aliases share the editor draft session. Embedded backup exports include live draft edits; import enters shared undo history and never publishes.

title: Measurement preferences
invariant: Convert physical measurements at the UI boundary. Browser-local unit preferences never rescale authored geometry; plan-coordinate inputs account for metersPerPlanUnit. Temperatures, angles and dimensionless values keep their own units. Settings → Editor owns units; Orbital view owns appearance, overlays, lighting and weather; Explore owns look controls. Stored preference keys remain compatible. Format metric diagnostic text only at the display boundary, including accessible labels, ranges and small clearances; quoted identifiers and deterministic validation output remain unchanged. Model-lighting movement labels follow the preference without changing physical steps.

title: Home Assistant agent relay
invariant: Commands decode inputs and call the same editing owners as the UI. Shipped pairing is HA-panel-only: the native authenticated WebSocket owns the editor subscription, while the CLI uses a short-lived Cabane relay token scoped to that workspace. No browser-to-localhost transport or HA credentials are given to the agent. Sessions and pending requests are ephemeral and invalidated on disconnect; history, validation and autosave remain editor-owned. The opt-in development runner uses isolated Chromium and a token-protected loopback endpoint to prepare disposable homes through the same executor; its bridge is omitted from production builds.

title: Construct and floor topology
invariant: Apartment floor settings live in Construct floor management and persist on the home; decorative shells never enter real floor lists or Walk geometry. Start at topology and validation for architectural changes: walls own openings; junctions and derived collision must agree. Optional door/window finish colors follow opening history and persistence without changing geometry. North orientation previews around the plan; only confirmation commits the shared building angle. Wall and Openings reuse EditorToolGroup for hover, click/tap and keyboard disclosure. Invisible wall reuses physical wall drawing and history, with dashed Construct-only strokes. Outdoor space selects the existing platform tool independently of Floor painting; tutorial and shortcut actions still select the original individual tools directly. Boundary (H) reuses hedge drawing, selection and persisted IDs. Wall edge color uses Auto or a persisted custom CSS color; Auto inherits matching authored side colors, then authored exterior color, otherwise the general interior wall finish. Face color controls follow wall direction and adjacent-room labels, preserve the opposite side, reset to the home palette, and highlight the edited face without persisting UI state. Wall niches remain wall-owned, preserve their backing through wall thickness edits and solid walk collision, and share placement, selection and resize gestures with doors and windows; Decorations groups Niche, Boundary and Pool. Solid room identities stay editable in Construct; runtime composition projects them into solidRooms outside navigation and mapping, with filled geometry and walk barriers. Wall and opening names preserve stable architectural and binding identities. Opening parsing lives in schema-opening.ts; wall types live in wall-types.ts. ConstructionInspector owns tool and building settings; ConstructionSelectionProperties owns selected-object attribute bodies in the shared inspector. Desktop tool disclosures and the mobile tool cards share construction-tool-options; choosing a mobile card returns to the canvas. Terrain corner heights are home-wide Construct edits using the ordinary project history and publication boundary. Terrain exit validation shares Walk’s step limit, accounts for supporting landings and reports non-blocking Issues with opening/platform Locate targets.

title: Arrange and placement
invariant: Resolve catalog definitions and supported placement before changing item records; preserve floor and item identity through history. Window-aware models use their declared opening types, including opt-in full-glass sliding doors without reclassifying architectural doors. Exterior-recessed window covers follow the window frame with catalog-owned closed opening clearance and derive controls from the opposite indoor wall face. project-runtime.ts owns ownerProjectExtensions, including catalog descriptors shared by editor preview, Connect and published-home composition, so room assignment remains consistent without saved overrides. Optional fabric colors follow item history and persistence; model defaultColor enables the picker. 3D elevation dragging preserves support and horizontal placement, commits one history step on release, and restores the initial placement on cancellation. Proportional resize dragging preserves placement, respects model resize policies, and shares the single-transaction commit/cancel behavior. Arrange edits and saved projects share scaled placement bounds; rejected moves/resizes retain the last accepted draft without a history step. Existing geometric placement problems warn while malformed data and structural references stay blocked. Explicit per-copy floor repairs preserve shared model normalization. The guarded reducer checks each queued result, including duplication; window fitting commits size and placement together. Furniture and devices author optional read-only attachments in Properties, sharing ordinary item history and publication.

title: Connect and binding profiles
invariant: Keep local slot declarations separate from browser household mappings; matching and rescan remain read-only. HA light helpers need no physical device; manual shared-light mappings retain every modeled slot. Connect retains standard room navigation and shared plan/sidebar connection counts, with progressively selected device and source panels and flat compatible source search including HA device names, and can add named sensor readings directly to scene devices or furniture, committing the local slot and private draft mapping in one history step. Explicit compatible choices can cross HA areas without an area prerequisite; automatic mapping stays area-scoped. Auxiliary sensor slots map independently across HA devices and areas, without changing or clearing the primary control. Manual TV switch alternatives are model-scoped and preserve existing slot identities.

title: Personal GLB models and asset transfer
invariant: Maintain the standalone authoring skill in .agents/skills/create-cabane-model alongside the product, retaining its MIT license and standalone installation. Keep personal import and illustrated AI-generation guidance inside Arrange's My models section. Manage models directly in its single preview grid, with hover, keyboard and touch access. Reuse the import preview for edits; preserve model/asset identity, copy scale and placement, and undo draft mapping cleanup with profile changes. Resolve personal definitions per project; validate self-contained GLBs and resource budgets before storage. Preserve materials, share and dispose resources, and publish verified assets before documents. Keep private bindings and authenticated transfers isolated by HA origin; interrupted transfers preserve the prior revision. Imported Light sources share the primary entity; selected emissive materials are instance-owned and physical emitter counts are bounded. Import and Edit use editCustomModel for one atomic definition, copy, lighting and draft binding update.

title: Home Assistant runtime and controls
invariant: Resolve and authorize supported controls at runtime; credentials and household IDs stay outside generated home source. Native sessions require matching HTTP or HTTPS page/host/workspace origins; standalone OAuth retains HTTPS or paired-loopback transport protection. Storage transfers remain bound to their originating authenticated session. Demo devices stay in memory, and simulated lights start on when the demo opens in night lighting while remaining manually controllable. Demo fans start at 50% speed and valves start open; normal controls update their in-memory state and existing catalog animations respect reduced motion.

title: Dashboard, navigation and cameras
invariant: Orbit and editor 3D share immediate, distance-based wheel zoom with cursor anchoring and a fixed navigation plane; 2D retains scroll-to-pan and pinch-to-zoom. Orbit light taps toggle one usable primary light; held dimming uses the continuous command channel and cancels on camera gestures or pointer loss, through the same guarded runtime in demo and connected homes. Room selection glides to a consistent angle fitted beside controls; manual navigation interrupts and retains active pointer listeners across dashboard re-renders, reduced motion settles immediately, and overview restores the device-local per-home/floor manual view. Reset explicitly restores default framing; Lock suppresses gestures and room reframing. The combined floor summary expands floor pills that update the active floor and room list; mobile keeps the floor pill and hides room pills. Keep floor switching and walk state coherent; missing runtime data must leave a usable scene. Room and device modules use content-sized cards and wrapping titles, with compact controls that preserve usable action targets. Sheet navigation puts actions on the left and Close on the right, retaining a left Back action only for nested device details; it overlays an edge-to-edge sticky parallax hero with reserved title clearance; mobile room sheets use a border and shadow with 54dvh height, coordinated with scene framing. Overlay preferences persist locally and filter only overview summaries. Area temperature/humidity readings take precedence over usable mapped room sensor fallbacks. RoomControlSheet and useRoomModuleOrder own browser-local per-home/room module order; RoomModuleReorder provides pointer, touch, and keyboard reordering without HA commands. Weather shares the Build/View tray and SceneActionButton rendering, uses matching sculpted icons and six preview choices (Live, Sunny, Cloudy, Rain, Thunderstorm, Snowy), defaults to Sunny with Live disabled when no HA weather entity exists, and applies only a visit-local scene override; it never changes HA state or the saved weather source. Room module projection deduplicates repeated single-entity light bindings into one room overview control while preserving each device for focused controls and scene rendering. Room cleaning reads HA vacuum area mappings on demand and sends one vacuum.clean_area request for the room’s explicitly mapped HA area; multiple matching robots require a selection. Room labels and item reading cards share SceneOverlayLayout collision selection and the viewport budget. Item states support Always, Never and Only if present, with conditional visibility based on fresh active or positive state. Opted-in item readings display independently of dashboard visibility; auxiliary telemetry never supplies ambient room status.

title: Scene geometry and rendering
invariant: The physicalFloor projection removes virtual walls and prunes their junction participants for rendering and Arrange supports. Architecture owns derived geometry and collision; the linked rendering contract defines finish, lighting, fade, shadow, and contour invariants. Near-wall lights retain point emission; the beauty pass masks receivers behind the wall's inner face in native batches and imported lit materials. Toon material preparation retains extension shader warmup. Authored geometry and hosted assets follow the visual-asset contract; personal GLBs use their dedicated import owner. Procedural wood preserves its pixels and batches canvas writes into one texture upload. Outline smoothing owns its derived geometry and preserves authored source normals. Custom terrain reveals basement facades, conforms grass, soil and outdoor finishes, preserves indoor/pool/stair cutouts and supplies rendered Walk heights. Zero heights preserve flat rendering; apartment shells suspend terrain overrides. Terrace slab coverage and floor/ceiling apertures share world-space clipping normalization, preserving saved coordinates and geometry holes.

title: Catalog and model extensions
invariant: Inspect stable registries first and consume public catalog subpaths. The linked catalog contract owns model placement, variants, activity, animation, and saved-project compatibility; home extensions own bespoke geometry. Mandatory surface verification covers all furnishing and device variants, including all four device connection states; flat artwork uses the engine LayeredSurface contract. Reusable additions exclude tiny standalone props and fitted apartment parts; square storage variants share one frame, and wall-mounted awnings retain wall support. Ordinary preset coverage uses shared catalog/surface checks and UI review. ArrangeCatalog owns category-card navigation, global search and model results on desktop and mobile; CatalogCategoryCards derives counts from the reusable entries.

title: Optional walk tools
invariant: Register optional tools in the web host; injected navigation, activation and storage keep HA access inside the engine. Prepare and retain shot shader programs on equip to avoid trigger-time compilation. The gun owns its first-use tutorial and browser-local dismissal. Engine targeting toggles one available light, fan, climate, media-player, switch or valve binding, preserving explicit slot scope and rejecting ambiguous targets.

title: Bundled home and agent generation
invariant: Author one accepted layout or room stage at a time in home/; browser edits do not rewrite the bundled seed. Follow the generation skill review gates.

title: Verification and delivery
invariant: AGENTS.md owns task sizing and local verification policy; the linked delivery contract documents command execution, CI, and HA release provenance. Test review follows docs/test-guidelines.md.

title: Shortcuts and private HA actions
invariant: Keep shortcut order and kinds portable; scene/script entity IDs belong to origin-scoped draft/published binding profiles. Save publishes both atomically. Activation uses guarded one-shot commands, never toggles. Outside-room devices are valid shortcut targets and open the existing non-spatial device control group without selecting a room. Shortcut edit controls wrap within their actual content container.

title: Engine UI styles
invariant: The public styles.css entry point owns explicit cascade order; global foundations live in styles/ and feature styles sit beside their React owners. Dashboard layout files and room-navigation.css coordinate cross-component responsive placement. Read room-navigation.css with room-control-sheet styles for room-focus changes. Extraction preserves selectors, declarations, media/container conditions, reduced-motion behavior and source order. React mounting order must not determine shared CSS precedence.

title: Shared model lighting
invariant: Keep one model lighting setup per home and one connection per placed copy. Preserve original furniture/device identity and controls. Native overrides never mutate the shared catalog. Source transforms and instance-owned glow use the same preview/runtime contract. Save and Undo include independent lighting identities and draft-only mapping cleanup; never operate HA during authoring. Preserve legacy declarations and mixed point/strip transforms. execution.ts alone bounds physical expansion for import, editor and floor runtime. Keep strips compact across copies; all logical sources contribute within the 64-light budget through fair strip sampling or spatial merging, without rewriting saved intent. Active sources take priority over native/dashboard prewarming; retain at most the bounded peak slots across state changes. Manifest validation accepts bounded compatibility emitters, including empty and zero-output settings. Broken optional runtime lighting is suppressed per model while geometry and saved definitions remain intact. Lighting recovery and approximation warnings use the existing editor Issues panel with per-item selection.
